summary.text: Brian A. Cunningham is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent in Assembly District 43, which covers Crown Heights, Prospect Lefferts Gardens, and Flatbush, and he has held the seat since winning a March 2022 special election.
A New York City native, he worked in nonprofit youth and anti-violence programs and as a staff member in the New York City Council and State Senate before entering the Assembly.
He won his June 2026 Democratic primary with 80.8% of the vote and is seeking re-election in November.

paragraphs.text: Cunningham was born and raised in New York City to Jamaican immigrant parents in a working-class family, according to his official biography.
He worked as a youth advisor with organizations including CAMBA and NPower, and as an aide to President Obama's My Brother's Keeper Alliance.
Ballotpedia describes his career as including work as an advocate counselor with CAMBA, as a senior aide in New York State legislative offices, and as director of Neighbors in Action.
According to his official biography, he was the first person elected to run a Cure Violence site in New York City, working to reduce gun violence in Central Brooklyn.
Before the Assembly he also served as Chief of Staff in the New York City Council and as a Special Assistant in the New York State Senate.

Cunningham won the March 22, 2022 special election for Assembly District 43 as the Democratic nominee, defeating Working Families Party candidate Jelanie DeShong with 62.28 percent of the vote, according to Board of Elections figures reported by Brooklyn Paper.
The seat was vacant because Diana Richardson had resigned to become a Deputy Borough President.
He took office on March 30, 2022, was elected to a full term in November 2022 on the Democratic and Working Families Party lines, and won the general election again in November 2024.

For the 2025-2026 session, Cunningham serves on the Assembly Agriculture, Banks, Codes, Consumer Affairs and Protection, Economic Development/Job Creation/Commerce and Industry, and Transportation Committees.

He is First Vice Chair of the New York State Association of Black, Puerto Rican, Hispanic & Asian Legislators, Inc., and was the inaugural Treasurer of the New York State Black Legislative Task Force.
His official biography says he has secured over $1 billion in state funding for the district since taking office, and that he lives in Brooklyn with his wife, Stephanie Cunningham, and their son.

sources.title: Brian Cunningham wins special election for Central Brooklyn Assembly seat
